title: A fair answer begins with understanding
meaning: You can hear each other more accurately when a considered distinction helps your answer match what was actually said rather than an attributed meaning.
text: On your Vishuddha, the Hermit in the physical position supports a thoughtful explanation: you show a distinction you have come to understand in a disagreement. Justice in energy seeks an honest relationship between words and response, without answering for something neither of you claimed. Justice in emotions means feeling understood without added assumptions. The wish for precision differs from the experience of fairness: an accurate quotation does not guarantee immediate relief.

For example, a disagreement includes “I dislike it when you finish my story”, while the reply becomes “You dislike talking to me altogether”. After reflection, you return to the difference between a particular habit and your conversation as a whole. **An answer becomes fairer when it keeps the request’s scale**. You can acknowledge an uncomfortable comment without expanding it into a judgement of closeness. The considered explanation helps you both see which words are actually being discussed and what needs an answer.

Difficulty arises if the explanation becomes an analysis of each other’s mistakes instead of an effort to understand. A technically precise objection may then feel like a new imbalance. The constructive wish for fairness helps bring your own tone into proportion with the request: clarifying meaning while allowing each other an emotional response. A sense of fair conversation grows through mutual participation as well as careful wording.
